Coverage¶

Summary¶

Coverage answers the area-coverage question: over this region and this time window, how many continuous reflection-track visits cross each cell? It lays a grid over a region (from a shapefile), then builds a track for every contiguous valid segment of every GNSS/LEO pair. Each cell crossed by a segment receives one visit. The result is a pass-count map, not a count of propagated time samples.

Both reflection geometries are supported: with reflection_type = "specular" (the default) the track is the specular-point line, and with "backscatter" it is the near-backscatter swath – the BRP track buffered by the ground half-width of the max_bistatic_bksc_angle_deg acceptance cone (see below).

This is a geometric measure: it depends only on the orbit and constellation geometry. The band’s frequency and EIRP feed only a finiteness check (is the reflection inside the antenna’s field of view), not a detect/no-detect threshold, so two bands of the same constellation give the same map. The band list therefore just selects which constellations take part. (Detectability-gated coverage, where the band would matter, is future work.)

Detailed Module Description¶

The grid¶

The region shapefile is turned into a grid of cells (a “fishnet”). An equidistant grid (cells a fixed number of metres across, *_gridded_m.shp) keeps cell area roughly constant; an equiangular grid (cells a fixed number of degrees, *_gridded_deg.shp) is simpler but its cells shrink toward the poles. The grid is generated once and cached next to the input shapefile, so later runs just load it.

Counting reflections¶

For each (LEO, GNSS) pair the specular reflections are found with Reflection. Consecutive valid samples form a LineString; an invalid or out-of-bounds sample splits the track into separate segments. A one-sample segment is kept as a Point. Every cell intersected by a segment receives at most one visit for that pair and segment, including cells crossed between propagated samples.

The track-visit count \(C\) for a cell is

(72)¶\[C_\mathrm{cell} = \sum_{\text{Tx, Rx, contiguous segment}} \mathbb{1}\big[\text{segment intersects cell and nearest-sample power is finite}\big],\]

The time, incidence angle and power stored for that visit come from the segment sample nearest the cell centroid; the crossing time is not interpolated. The finite-power condition acts as the antenna field-of-view gate. The band changes neither geometric term’s truth value, which is why coverage is per constellation.

Backscatter coverage (the near-backscatter swath)¶

With reflection_type = "backscatter" the track is the BRP line (BRP): the point where the straight line through the transmitter and the receiver meets the surface – exact retroreflection, bistatic angle \(\beta = 0\). Exact alignment is a zero-width condition, so a cell counts as covered while its bistatic angle – the angle at the cell between the directions to the transmitter and to the receiver – stays below the acceptance half-angle \(\beta_\mathrm{max}\) ([COVERAGE].max_bistatic_bksc_angle_deg). A surface point displaced by \(d\) across the shared line of sight opens the bistatic angle by \(\beta \simeq d\,(1/R_r - 1/R_t)\) (both satellites sit on the same side of the surface, hence the difference of curvatures), so the acceptance region around the BRP has cross-LOS half-width

(73)¶\[w = \frac{\beta_\mathrm{max}}{1/R_r - 1/R_t} \qquad \left(\approx 92\ \mathrm{km\ for\ } \beta_\mathrm{max}=5^\circ \mathrm{\ at\ a\ 700\ km\ orbit}\right),\]

with slant ranges \(R_r\) (surface to receiver) and \(R_t\) (surface to transmitter). The BRP track is buffered by the segment-minimum \(w\) – the conservative, smaller semi-axis of the acceptance ellipse (the in-plane axis is wider by \(1/\cos\theta_i\)) – before the cell intersection; segmentation, the one-visit-per-segment rule and the finite-power antenna gate are identical to the specular path. \(\beta_\mathrm{max} = 5^\circ\) matches the ocean RCS model’s near-backscatter Bragg gate, so “covered” then means “sees the geometry the backscatter clutter model itself calls backscatter”.

class object_definitions.Coverage_def.Coverage(sat_const, gnss_const, shapefile, grid_size_deg=None, grid_size_m=None, overwrite_shapefile=False, earth_model='spherical', link_budget_settings=None, *, max_central_angle_deg, selected_signals=None, reflection_type='specular', max_incidence_angle_deg=None, max_bistatic_bksc_angle_deg=None)[source]¶

Count contiguous reflection-track visits per grid cell over a region (the area-coverage mode).

Builds (or loads) a gridded version of an input shapefile, then – per GNSS constellation – connects each contiguous run of valid samples into a track and counts one visit per intersected cell and run. In specular mode the track is the specular-point line; in backscatter mode it is the BRP track buffered by the near-backscatter swath (all cells whose bistatic angle to some (Tx, Rx) pair stays below max_bistatic_bksc_angle_deg). Coverage is a geometric metric: the band’s frequency and EIRP only feed the antenna-field-of-view finiteness gate, not a detection threshold, so the result is per constellation, not per band.

Parameters:

  • sat_const (SatelliteConstellation) – LEO receiver constellation.

  • gnss_const (dict) – {name: SatelliteConstellation} of GNSS transmitter constellations.

  • shapefile (str) – Path to the region shapefile (the grid is generated alongside it).

  • grid_size_deg (float or None, optional) – Cell size in degrees (equiangular grid). Mutually exclusive with grid_size_m.

  • grid_size_m (float or None, optional) – Cell size in metres (equidistant grid).

  • overwrite_shapefile (bool, optional) – Regenerate the gridded shapefile even if it exists.

  • earth_model ({"spherical", "elliptical"}, optional) – Surface model for the reflection geometry.

  • link_budget_settings (dict or BistaticLinkBudgetSettings or None, optional) – Rx-system link-budget settings (used only for the finiteness gate).

  • max_central_angle_deg (float, keyword-only) – Maximum Tx-Rx central angle [deg].

  • selected_signals (list of dict or None, keyword-only) – Validated INI band plan; deduplicated to one entry per constellation.

  • reflection_type ({"specular", "backscatter"}, keyword-only) – Reflection geometry the coverage counts (default “specular”).

  • max_incidence_angle_deg (float or None, keyword-only) – Maximum BRP incidence angle [deg]; required for backscatter.

  • max_bistatic_bksc_angle_deg (float or None, keyword-only) – Maximum bistatic angle at the surface for a cell to count as near-backscatter-covered [deg]; sets the swath half-width around the BRP track. Required for backscatter, unused for specular.

Module Assumptions and Limitations¶

  • Geometric metric. Coverage counts reflections, not detections; the band’s frequency/EIRP only gate finiteness. Per-band coverage is meaningless until a detection threshold is added.

  • Conservative backscatter swath. The swath uses the cross-LOS half-width (the smaller semi-axis of the acceptance ellipse), the segment-minimum radius, and the degree-of-latitude conversion for the isotropic buffer, so the counted swath never overstates the \(\beta\) acceptance region – it slightly understates its in-plane and east-west extent.

  • Grid choice matters. Equiangular cells distort with latitude; use the equidistant (metre) grid for area-fair counts.

  • Track-intersection counting. Counts are one per contiguous Tx/Rx track segment crossing a cell, not one per time sample. Results can change with propagation cadence because straight lines interpolate between samples and invalid samples split passes.

  • No footprint spreading. Only the specular track (or the \(\beta\)-acceptance swath in backscatter) is intersected with cells; the receiver antenna footprint is not distributed across neighbouring cells.

  • Approximate visit metadata. Stored times, angles and powers are those of the sample nearest the cell centroid, not an interpolated boundary-crossing event.

Validation and Tests¶

Test module

What it pins

tests/test_coverage.py

Grid generation and loading, bounding-box handling for both grid types, preservation of singleton and separated contiguous runs, per-cell counting, and the statistics summary; the backscatter swath half-width (analytic anchors, distant-transmitter limit) and the swath-vs-thin-track cell counts (a synthetic BRP track covers the neighbouring cell column that the thin line misses).

User Guide¶

This is the class behind python SRC/main_simulation_areaCoverage.py (configured by Configuration_area.ini). The relevant INI pieces:

  • [COVERAGE].shapefile_path – the region outline.

  • [COVERAGE].grid_size_meters (or a degree size) – the cell size.

  • [REFLECTION].reflection_type – "specular" (default) or "backscatter"; backscatter also requires [REFLECTION].max_incidence_angle_deg.

  • [COVERAGE].max_bistatic_bksc_angle_deg – the near-backscatter acceptance half-angle (required for backscatter, unused for specular).

  • [ANTENNA].bands – selects which constellations take part.

  • [ORBITS] / [GNSS CONSTELLATIONS] – the receiver and transmitter fleets.

References¶

  • Jales, P. & Unwin, M., “Mission description – GNSS Reflectometry on TDS-1 with the SGR-ReSI”, SSTL, 2015.
